chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: 'Up In Dodo's Room' and his influence on Coltrane's generation
summary: His McGhee recording for Tempo; Fats Navarro said the solo broke from the Young and Hawkins schools, and Coltrane and others studied it.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: ...back in New York when he decided to move here.
Tempo Records was there just about... It was near Van Ness and Hollywood Boulevard, right along in there.
Is that where Lee Wiley later (?)?

Right. See, that's the same place. Lee Wiley was working for him, and he eventually sold it to her when he moved to New York to set up shop in New York. Now, that's where he was when we recorded for him. Howard McGhee... We made his second outing. And that's where I made what I later on found out to be a classic recording, "Up In Dodo's Room," with Howard McGhee's band. Dodo Marmarosa, the great pianist, was playing piano. And I didn't realize that the solo had any significance until I met Fats Navarro, the great trumpet player, in 1948. "Look," he said, "do you realize that you changed the course of history?" I said, "What are you talking about, I changed the course of history?" He said, "Well, your solo on 'Up In

Dodo's Room' was the first solo of any tenor saxophone player that hadn't come from the Lester Young or the Coleman Hawkins school. Everybody else came from one of those schools." He said, "You were the first one to do it different" on that solo in 1945 -- "Up In Dodo's Room." Because that particular solo, if I remember correctly, had all the half-steps in it. It had the major-seventh, which was just beginning to get popular. It had the flat nine; I played the flat nines. I played all the hip stuff that they call hip today; I played it in 1945.

Yeah. Later on, I found out that John Coltrane and Jimmy Heath and Jackie McLean and Sonny Rollins and a lot of other guys had been studying me from out here. Milt Jackson, Percy Heath, all those guys could sing those solos note-for-note, and I couldn't even sing them! [LAUGHS HEARTILY]
